role: fresh citation and claim verifier, independent of the slate owner and the discovery cells; edits limited to recording verdicts
boundary: Citation and claim verification only. Checks that each registry claim matches its primary source or the repository; it does not judge novelty, significance or design, and it is not a gauntlet score.

verdict_legend.VERIFIED: the primary source or repository record says what the claim says (qualifiers in 'note')
verdict_legend.CORRECTED: the claim is wrong or mis-scoped; 'fix' gives the corrected statement
verdict_legend.UNVERIFIABLE: no retained source or derivation to check against; keep it labelled provisional or as an estimate
verdict_legend.REMOVED: unsupported and should come out of the slate (none)

method: arXiv: abs page (title, version history, comments, journal ref) and the PDF converted with pdftotext -layout for all 101 cited ids; figures searched in the text.
OpenReview: api2 notes/search with source=forum for all 10 cited forum ids; abstracts read from search results. Per-note fetch returns ChallengeRequiredError (403) and was not bypassed.
DOIs: Crossref works API; doi.org redirect checked for one.
Hugging Face: API metadata only (licence tags, file lists, LFS oids); no dataset download. Cell-3 scratch parquets were used only after their SHA-256 matched the HF LFS oids.
Repository: every cited file read at the cited lines; a1.jsonl, report-guarded.json, s15.json and evaluator-diff.json recounted with the Python standard library.
No host job, no GPU, no recursive search of the session scratchpad.

slate_text_findings.finding: 'Desktop file-state checkers are untested in every prior found, and 2610.09142 says so': 2610.09142's 'remain untested' sentence is in its Limitations and describes its own two-suite scope. Suggested wording: '2610.09142 names OSWorld-Verified-class desktop checkers as outside its scope (Limitations) and lists an OSWorld rank-consequence audit as future work.' The absence claim rests on the cells' searches, not on that paper.
2610.04433: the 13% flip rate (swap and rerun alike) is the median on a 45-task hard subset of SWE-bench Verified with five models (see c095).
2609.21058's 4 of 60 is at the 1e-2 (bf16) tolerance; at that harness's fp32 tolerance (1e-4) it is 2 of 60. R11's protocol is allclose at 1e-2, so the figure applies; add the qualifier.

'389 of 390 accepted drkernel kernels that call tl.dot use its TF32 default': what was counted is that they pass no explicit non-TF32 precision; TF32 applies only when operands are fp32, which was not checked (see c187).

KBV's contribution list says TF32 is enabled 'in the PyTorch reference' for the performance baseline, and describes the change as substituting baseline timing; it does not state the correctness reference's precision separately. The slate's reading is defensible; cite that sentence and keep the plan to read the released harness.
